benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Structured prompt topologies with Bayesian path pruning can filter distracting or irrelevant retrieved documents to improve RAG accuracy under noisy context. | Parallel processing of independent document paths enables both acceleration and noise filtering for long-context RAG.
limitation_or_note: Focus is primarily on efficiency rather than reliability; pruning is evaluated on standard QA datasets without explicit adversarial or unreliable-evidence stress tests.

title: Two-tiered Encoder-based Hallucination Detection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Wild
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
benchmark_or_task: other
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Two-tiered encoder classifiers that first filter non-verifiable statements and then check support against retrieved KB can outperform LLM-based hallucination detection in production RAG. | Combining a small amount of in-domain data with public NLI/hallucination datasets meaningfully improves grounding/faithfulness detection in enterprise RAG settings. | Encoder NLI models can be more cost-effective and accurate than decoder LLMs for sentence-level RAG faithfulness checking.
limitation_or_note: Industry-track applied paper focused on customer service domains; results may not generalize and the work does not propose new abstention/control mechanisms inside the RAG generator itself.

title: ChatQA 2: Bridging the Gap to Proprietary LLMs in Long Context and RAG Capabilities
authors: Peng Xu; Wei Ping; Xianchao Wu; Chejian Xu; Zihan Liu; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Long-context RAG benefits from long-context retrievers that reduce chunk fragmentation, with accuracy improving as the number of retrieved tokens grows. | Empirical comparisons between direct long-context and RAG show RAG can match or surpass strong long-context LLMs when sufficient top-k chunks are provided.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on capability extension and accuracy comparison, not on robustness under noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence.

title: ChatQA: Surpassing GPT-4 on Conversational QA and RAG
authors: Zihan Liu; Wei Ping; Rajarshi Roy; Peng Xu; Chankyu Lee; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Conversational RAG benchmarks like ChatRAG Bench enable evaluation of grounding, table reasoning, and unanswerable handling across diverse document types. | Incorporating a small amount of unanswerable training samples significantly improves a RAG model's ability to abstain rather than hallucinate when evidence is insufficient. | Fine-tuning single-turn retrievers on conversational query-context pairs can match LLM-based query rewriters for multi-turn retrieval without extra inference cost.
limitation_or_note: The paper's main goal is matching GPT-4 on conversational QA rather than systematically studying unreliable evidence; the unanswerable evaluation is a single component, so it should not be overclaimed as a robustness method.

title: Do Metadata and Appearance of the Retrieved Webpages Affect LLM's Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
benchmark_or_task: other
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Non-textual metadata such as publication date and webpage appearance can causally shift LLM answers under conflicting retrieved evidence, even when source credibility cues are largely ignored. | Conflicting-evidence RAG outcomes depend on signals beyond textual content, motivating robustness analyses that consider metadata manipulation as an adversarial surface.
limitation_or_note: Small sample (355+125 questions), single metadata type per experiment, and no proposed defense or training method; findings are descriptive rather than prescriptive.

title: Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
benchmark_or_task: domain_biomed_legal_finance
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: LLMs exhibit pseudo-helpfulness by generating answers even when gold documents are absent from retrieved context, a key failure mode under unreliable evidence | RAG generation quality degrades with more distractor documents and is sensitive to gold document position in the retrieved list, motivating re-ranking and noise filtering | Instruction following and prompt robustness vary substantially across model families, affecting reliability of RAG deployments in domain-specific settings
limitation_or_note: Proprietary financial datasets are not released, limiting reproducibility; findings are based on a relatively narrow model set (GPT-3.5/4 and Llama-2 variants) from 2024 and may not generalize.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
authors:
Lionel Wong, Ayman Ali, Raymond M Xiong, Zejiang Shen, Yoon Kim, Monica Agrawal;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:82347-82359
benchmark_or_task: domain_biomed_legal_finance
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RAG systems can be 'pragmatically misaligned'—producing literally accurate but contextually misleading content by decontextualizing facts, omitting balance, and reinforcing query biases | Robust RAG evaluation in high-stakes domains must look beyond factual accuracy and citation grounding to assess source-intent fidelity and downstream user interpretation | Production RAG search systems exhibit query-valence sensitivity, selecting different evidence from the same sources depending on how a question is framed
limitation_or_note: Position paper with qualitative/quantitative observational analysis on two commercial systems rather than a controlled benchmark or new method; claims should be cited as motivating evidence, not as a rigorous evaluation suite.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
authors: Xiaoqian Shen; Wenxuan Zhang; Jun Chen; Mohamed Elhoseiny
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Graph-based RAG with structured post-retrieval reasoning can filter hard-negative retrieved clips and mitigate noise in long-video understanding. | Even when correct evidence is retrieved, LVLMs can be distracted by irrelevant retrieved clips, motivating verification and refinement steps in multimodal RAG.
limitation_or_note: Scope is limited to long-video QA benchmarks and does not formally evaluate adversarial or poisoned evidence, so its contribution to unreliable-evidence robustness is implicit rather than direct.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
authors: Haidong Xu; Guangwei Xu; Zhedong Zheng; Xiatian Zhu; Wei Ji; Xiangtai Li; Ruijie Guo; Meishan Zhang; Min zhang; Hao Fei
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Cross-modal RAG pipelines (e.g., video-to-3D-motion) suffer from error propagation when retrieved evidence is noisy or misaligned with the target modality. | Preference-based training (DPO with dual-alignment rewards) can teach generators to discount non-informative retrieved evidence and adaptively rely on retrieval quality.
limitation_or_note: The work is specific to text-to-motion generation; generalization of McDPO-style robustness to text-only or other modalities is not directly validated, so overclaiming its method as a general robust-RAG technique should be avoided.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
authors: Tsung-Han Wu; Giscard Biamby; Jerome Quenum; Ritwik Gupta; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Trevor Darrell; David Chan
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Multi-image visual RAG requires filtering of irrelevant images to avoid distractor-induced degradation in LMM reasoning. | Vision-centric needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks reveal LMM weaknesses including positional bias and poor cross-image reasoning under unreliable visual evidence.
limitation_or_note: The benchmark is template-based on COCO objects and may inherit COCO biases; findings on distractor robustness may not generalize to open-domain multimodal RAG.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shicheng Xu; Liang Pang; Huawei Shen; Xueqi Cheng
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Token-level fusion between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence can be theoretically decomposed into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction). | The actual effect of RAG on each token can be predicted from representation similarity without training or external utility evaluators, enabling adaptive token-level use of retrieved evidence. | Training-free collaborative decoding between pure LLM and RAG improves robustness to noisy retrieved passages across QA and long-form tasks.
limitation_or_note: Theory rests on strong latent-variable/HMM assumptions and the practical method depends on heuristics for locating the 'distribution fusion' layer.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Automated RAG evaluation frameworks decompose quality into context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance, using fine-tuned LLM judges over synthetic query-passage-answer triples. | Prediction-powered inference enables tighter confidence intervals on RAG performance using a small human-annotated validation set combined with judge predictions on unlabeled data. | Lightweight fine-tuned judges generalize across in-domain shifts but degrade under drastic shifts (cross-lingual, text-to-code), motivating evaluation-time robustness considerations.
limitation_or_note: ARES targets general English RAG evaluation and does not specifically test adversarial, poisoned, or knowledge-conflict scenarios that are central to unreliable-evidence robustness; judges also degrade under large domain shifts.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Active retrieval that triggers based on generation-time confidence (low token probability) outperforms fixed-interval or single-shot retrieval in long-form generation. | Forward-looking queries formed from the anticipated next sentence are more effective than past-context queries for adaptive RAG. | Masking low-confidence tokens or generating targeted sub-questions mitigates error propagation when using model-generated content as retrieval queries.
limitation_or_note: Calibration assumption (low probability == knowledge gap) may not hold for newer LLMs; the paper does not directly study adversarial or poisoned evidence robustness.

title: An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Information bottleneck objectives can train noise filters that simultaneously maximize useful information and minimize irrelevant retrieved content for RAG. | IB-based filtering can produce empty compressions when retrieved passages are irrelevant, supporting abstention-like behavior under unreliable evidence. | IB provides a unified principle for evaluation metrics, SFT data selection, and RL reward design in noise filtering.
limitation_or_note: Method depends on white-box LLM probability access for the IB metric and operates only at the extractive filtering level; abstention behavior is heuristic via an additional discard flag.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tobias Leemann; Periklis Petridis; Giuseppe Vietri; Dionysis Manousakas; Aaron Roth; Sergul Aydore
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Lightweight NLI-based grounding verifiers can be domain-adapted via synthetic data to detect ungrounded RAG outputs at low latency | Iterative synthetic data generation with weak teacher labels and label-preserving augmentations closes most of the domain gap for grounding verification in RAG
limitation_or_note: The paper assumes covariate shift only and access to a representative target-domain evidence corpus; it does not directly study adversarial or poisoned evidence, so reliability claims under malicious unreliable evidence should not be overstated.

title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: BEIR provides a heterogeneous zero-shot retrieval benchmark spanning 18 datasets and 9 tasks, exposing that in-domain retrieval performance does not predict out-of-distribution generalization—a core concern for RAG retrievers facing unreliable or domain-shifted evidence. | Analysis of annotation selection bias (e.g., lexical bias in TREC-COVID) demonstrates that retrieval evaluation itself can be unreliable, motivating careful evaluation protocols for evidence quality in RAG. | BM25 remains a strong zero-shot baseline while dense retrievers can underperform on shifted domains, informing retriever choice and robustness considerations in RAG pipelines.
limitation_or_note: BEIR evaluates retrievers in isolation rather than end-to-end RAG with generators, and is English-only with limited long-document and multi-field coverage; survey should not present it as a full RAG benchmark.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
authors: Yangning Li; Yinghui Li; Xinyu Wang; Yong Jiang; Zhen Zhang; Xinran Zheng; Hui Wang; Hai-Tao Zheng; Fei Huang; Jingren Zhou; Philip S. Yu
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Heuristic multimodal RAG with fixed two-step retrieval fails on dynamic, multi-hop, or multimodal-knowledge questions because of non-adaptive and overloaded retrieval queries. | Self-adaptive planning agents that decompose complex multimodal questions into sub-question chains and dynamically choose retrieval tools (image/text search) improve robustness over rigid mRAG pipelines. | Dyn-VQA provides a benchmark for evaluating mRAG under rapidly changing answers, cross-modal knowledge needs, and >2-hop reasoning.
limitation_or_note: Evaluation depends on commercial search APIs and proprietary MLLM backbones; F1-recall metric and small benchmark size (~1.5K) limit statistical robustness.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
benchmark_or_task: domain_biomed_legal_finance
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Domain-specific RAG benchmarks (e.g., MIRAGE for medicine) reveal that retriever/corpus/LLM choices have large and task-dependent effects on answer accuracy. | Medical RAG exhibits log-linear scaling with the number of retrieved snippets and a 'lost-in-the-middle' effect on the position of the ground-truth snippet, highlighting context-use robustness issues. | Combining heterogeneous corpora and fusing retrievers (e.g., RRF) tends to improve robustness across diverse medical QA tasks.
limitation_or_note: The work focuses on multi-choice medical QA with vanilla prepend-RAG, so its conclusions may not transfer to open-ended generation, adversarial/poisoned evidence, or non-medical domains.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
authors: Wenbin An; Jiahao Nie; Feng Tian; Haonan Lin; mingxiang cai; Yaqiang Wu; QianYing Wang; Xiaoqin Zhang; Shijian Lu
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Multimodal RAG systems suffer from attention bias toward visual tokens and knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge, requiring adaptive mechanisms to balance the two when retrieved evidence varies in reliability. | Training-free decoding interventions that adaptively reweight parametric vs contextual logits based on attention-derived reliability signals can mitigate unreliable retrieval in MLLMs.
limitation_or_note: Method is decoding-only and assumes white-box access to MLLM parameters; evaluation focuses on knowledge-intensive VQA benchmarks rather than adversarial or poisoned retrieval settings.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Liang Wang; Haonan Chen; Nan Yang; Xiaolong Huang; Zhicheng Dou; Furu Wei
benchmark_or_task: other
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Iterative chain-of-retrieval with learned query reformulation improves robustness when single-step retrieval fails on complex multi-hop queries. | Test-time compute can be adaptively scaled (chain length, best-of-N, tree search, learning-to-stop) to control the trade-off between answer quality and retrieval reliability. | Trained iterative retrievers remain robust across retrievers of varying quality (E5-large, E5-base, BM25), indicating partial decoupling from retriever noise.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on short-answer multi-hop QA and KILT tasks; does not directly evaluate adversarial or poisoned evidence, and benefits diminish on simple single-hop queries.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Dynamic/adaptive RAG can decide when to retrieve based on token-level uncertainty, attention importance, and semantic content rather than fixed rules. | Query formulation that leverages self-attention over the full generated context can better capture the model's real-time information needs than using only the last sentence or last few tokens. | Unnecessary retrieval can introduce noisy evidence and harm generation quality, motivating selective/adaptive retrieval triggers.
limitation_or_note: The method requires access to internal self-attention scores, limiting applicability to API-only LLMs; evaluation is limited to knowledge-intensive QA and does not test under adversarial or corrupted-corpus conditions.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Wenxuan Shi; Haochen Tan; Chuqiao Kuang; Xiaoguang Li; Hanting Chen; Xiaozhe Ren; Yasheng Wang; Lu Hou; Lifeng Shang
benchmark_or_task: agent_memory_tool
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RL-trained adaptive search intensity scaling enables LLMs to escalate retrieval depth and frequency when facing noisy or unreliable open-web evidence | Real-world open-web RAG benchmarks (WebPuzzle) elicit information-seeking behaviors such as conflict resolution, verification, and reflection that clean Wiki-based benchmarks under-test
limitation_or_note: Experiments are constrained to 7B backbones and a primarily Chinese open-web setting; generalization claims to English/larger models rely on translated subsets.

title: Do You Know What You Are Talking About? Characterizing Query-Knowledge Relevance For Reliable Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: domain_biomed_legal_finance
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Goodness-of-fit hypothesis testing over query-document similarity statistics can detect out-of-knowledge queries and trigger abstention in RAG systems. | Synthetic in-knowledge queries generated from corpus chunks can approximate the true in-knowledge distribution for calibrating rejection thresholds. | Embedding models' retrieval accuracy can be misaligned with their ability to detect out-of-knowledge queries, motivating separate diagnostics.
limitation_or_note: Experiments are concentrated in biomedical QA with relatively small subsets (300 samples), and synthetic queries may be overly simple compared to real user queries, which limits the generality of the empirical conclusions.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Zhenting Qi; Hanlin Zhang; Eric P. Xing; Sham M. Kakade; Himabindu Lakkaraju
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RAG datastores are vulnerable to prompt-injection-based extraction attacks that exploit instruction-following capabilities of LMs. | Position bias and ineffective context utilization are root causes of datastore leakage, and position-invariant inference combined with safety-aware prompting mitigates the attack. | Production RAG systems such as customized GPTs can leak verbatim datastore content at high rates with minimal queries.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on datastore privacy leakage rather than answer correctness under noisy/poisoned evidence, so framing should not overextend it to general retrieval noise robustness.

title: Generate-then-Ground in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-hop Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Generate-then-ground frameworks can mitigate noise in retrieved documents by alternating LLM answer generation with evidence-based revision. | Batch grounding strategies and instructional grounding distillation help LLMs ignore plausible-looking but irrelevant retrieved content in multi-hop QA.
limitation_or_note: Evaluation is limited to multi-hop QA with Wikipedia corpora and does not explicitly stress-test adversarial or counterfactual noise beyond standard retrieval imperfections.

title: Influence Guided Context Selection for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiale Deng; Yanyan Shen; Ziyuan Pei; Youmin Chen; Linpeng Huang
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Context selection based on holistic quality assessment (query-, list-, and generator-aware) can effectively filter noisy/irrelevant retrieved contexts and improve RAG robustness. | Reframing context quality as an inference-time data valuation problem (Contextual Influence value) enables hyperparameter-free selection by retaining only contexts with positive marginal contribution. | A lightweight surrogate model trained with oracle influence supervision plus end-to-end generator feedback can approximate expensive influence computations at inference.
limitation_or_note: CSM currently requires task-specific training with oracle CI value supervision; cross-task generalization and scaling to very large context lists are not fully demonstrated.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
authors: Zhepei Wei; Wei-Lin Chen; Yu Meng
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Self-synthesized rationales can train LMs to explicitly denoise noisy retrieved contexts, improving robustness to imperfect retrievers. | Explicit rationale-based denoising scales better with more retrieved documents than vanilla RAG, mitigating performance degradation under high noise ratios. | Instruction-tuning-style rationale supervision generalizes across in-domain and out-of-domain RAG tasks without extra human annotation.
limitation_or_note: Evaluation is largely confined to QA benchmarks and depends on substring/LLM-judge metrics; generalization to open-ended generation or adversarial poisoning is not directly tested.

title: LaRA: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Long-Context LLMs – No Silver Bullet for LC or RAG Routing
authors:
Kuan Li, Liwen Zhang, Yong Jiang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Shuai Wang, Minhao Cheng;

benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: LaRA provides a rigorous benchmark for comparing RAG and long-context LLMs across four task types (location, reasoning, comparison, hallucination detection) and shows no universal winner. | RAG's relative benefit depends on model strength, context length, and task type, with RAG outperforming LC for weaker models and longer contexts, and notably for hallucination detection. | LC LLMs exhibit lost-in-the-middle behavior while RAG is more robust to answer position, motivating routing strategies under unreliable evidence.
limitation_or_note: Findings are tied to a specific RAG configuration and QA-only tasks; conclusions about RAG vs LC routing may not generalize to other retrievers, generative tasks, or noisy/adversarial corpora.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Long-context RAG suffers from chunking-induced loss of global structure and low evidence density, motivating extractor-plus-filter pipelines. | CoT-guided filtering combined with mapping chunks back to source paragraphs can reduce noise and improve robustness over Self-RAG and CRAG on multi-hop QA.
limitation_or_note: Authors note dependence on one-time retrieval quality and potential annotation bias from LLM-generated fine-tuning data; gains are reported on three multi-hop datasets only.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: LLMs exhibit a U-shaped position bias when using retrieved evidence, performing worst when relevant information appears in the middle of long input contexts. | Reader performance saturates well before retriever recall in open-domain QA, indicating that adding more retrieved documents yields diminishing returns and motivates reranking or truncation for robust RAG. | Extended-context models are not necessarily better at using their input context, complicating naive scaling solutions for evidence-rich RAG pipelines.
limitation_or_note: Findings are tied to specific 2023-era models and prompt formats; later models with improved long-context training may exhibit mitigated but not eliminated positional bias.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
authors: Peng Xia; Kangyu Zhu; Haoran Li; Tianze Wang; Weijia Shi; Sheng Wang; Linjun Zhang; James Zou; Huaxiu Yao
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Multimodal medical RAG systems must handle domain heterogeneity via domain-aware retrievers and adaptively select the number of retrieved contexts to avoid noise-induced hallucinations. | Preference fine-tuning targeting cross-modality alignment and over-reliance on retrieved evidence mitigates two distinct RAG failure modes (copy-reference and retrieval interference) in vision-language models. | Diagnostic metrics such as Copy-Reference rate and Over-Reliance rate provide useful evaluation tools for measuring RAG robustness under unreliable retrieved evidence.
limitation_or_note: Scope is limited to medical VLMs and the preference-pair construction depends on the base model already producing some correct vs. incorrect responses; generalization beyond medical imaging is not fully validated.

title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
authors: Maojia Song; Shang Hong Sim; Rishabh Bhardwaj; Hai Leong Chieu; Navonil Majumder; Soujanya Poria
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Alignment via DPO with paired positive/negative responses can substantially improve LLMs' ability to refuse unanswerable RAG queries and ground answers in retrieved documents. | Holistic trustworthiness metrics combining grounded refusals, calibrated answer correctness, and citation precision/recall expose how parametric-knowledge reliance inflates standard RAG scores. | Disentangling retriever quality from LLM groundedness is necessary to measure robust behavior under insufficient or irrelevant evidence.
limitation_or_note: Evaluation centers on ASQA/QAMPARI/ELI5/ExpertQA and relies on a TRUE-based NLI judge for answerability, which may not generalize to multimodal, agentic, or adversarial unreliable-evidence settings.

title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Model internals (gradient-based saliency over context tokens) can produce more faithful answer attributions in RAG than self-citation prompting or external NLI validators. | Self-citation and NLI-based attribution are brittle under instruction-following failures and surface lexical overlap, motivating internals-based faithfulness checks for trustworthy RAG.
limitation_or_note: Evaluated only on 7B open-source LLMs and uses NLI (TRUE) as a proxy reference on ELI5, which the authors acknowledge as a brittleness limitation; generalization to larger models and broader domains is not demonstrated.

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
authors:
Chenyang Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jian Lou, Kai Wu, Zilong Wang, Xiaofeng Chen;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:76811-76830
benchmark_or_task: vision_multimodal
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Vision-language RAG systems are vulnerable to single-sample knowledge poisoning attacks that manipulate target responses by jointly crafting poison images and texts to satisfy retrievability and inducibility. | Class-targeted multimodal poisoning extends attack reach beyond exact-match queries, and standard defenses like noise, cropping, and RoCLIP only partially mitigate such attacks. | Robust RAG must consider multimodal evidence integrity, since perturbations to retrieval embeddings can cause poisoned image-text pairs to dominate top-K retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Strongest variants (PoisonedEye-S/C) assume white-box access to the retriever; evaluation focuses on a single multimodal database (OVEN-Wiki) and a narrow target-response style.

title: Provence: efficient and robust context pruning for retrieval-augmented generation
authors: Nadezhda Chirkova; Thibault Formal; Vassilina Nikoulina; Stéphane CLINCHANT
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Context pruning via sequence labeling can dynamically remove irrelevant retrieved sentences and improve robustness to noisy evidence in RAG. | Unifying reranking and context pruning into a single cross-encoder yields near-zero-cost evidence filtering that generalizes across QA domains and context lengths.
limitation_or_note: Scope limited to English QA with single-passage processing; gains depend on the chosen threshold and silver-label LLM quality, and the unified reranking head adds a small trade-off versus standalone rerankers.

title: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards
authors: Xinze Li; Sen Mei; Zhenghao Liu; Yukun Yan; Shuo Wang; Shi Yu; Zheni Zeng; Hao Chen; Ge Yu; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun; Chenyan Xiong
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Differentiable preference-based training (DPO with rollout rewards) can align data preferences across RAG modules and mitigate knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence. | End-to-end optimization of the generation module improves robustness to noisy retrieved documents and reduces overfitting compared to SFT-based RAG training (e.g., RA-DIT).
limitation_or_note: Improvements on knowledge refinement are limited; effectiveness is shown mainly on standard knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, not on adversarial/poisoned corpora.

title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-form Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: medium
actual_contribution: Cross-domain robustness evaluation for RAG-QA requires long-form coherent reference answers that integrate evidence across multiple documents rather than short extractive spans. | LLM-as-judge pairwise evaluation against human-written long-form references can serve as a scalable, reliable benchmark for RAG-QA systems across diverse domains.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on answer-quality evaluation and domain robustness rather than directly on adversarial or noisy evidence robustness; LLM-judge bias and cost are acknowledged limitations.

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Reference-free metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance enable automated assessment of RAG pipelines when ground-truth annotations are unavailable. | LLM-based decomposition into atomic statements and verification against retrieved context can diagnose grounding failures and unreliable evidence use in RAG systems. | Dedicated evaluation toolkits (RAGAs) and datasets (WikiEval) provide standardized infrastructure for measuring how robustly RAG systems handle context relevance and faithfulness.
limitation_or_note: Metrics depend on a closed LLM judge and were validated on a small (50-page) WikiEval set, so reported human-agreement numbers may not transfer to harder evidence-conflict or adversarial settings.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
authors:
Jennifer Hsia, Afreen Shaikh, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Graham Neubig;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:24139-24155
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Reader robustness to noisy retrieval, rather than retriever quality alone, is the dominant factor governing RAG stability and scalability across retrieval depths. | Systematic evaluation metrics like RAG Stability Score (RSS) and RAG Scalability Coefficient (RSC) provide principled diagnostics of RAG behavior under realistic, non-oracle retrieval conditions. | Prompting interventions for noise filtering are inconsistent and cannot substitute for reranking or reader noise robustness, particularly in specialized domains.
limitation_or_note: Evaluation is limited to QA-style benchmarks (NQ, HotpotQA, BioASQ, preliminary CRAG) and does not cover adversarial or poisoned evidence; metrics emphasize aggregate stability rather than per-instance failure modes.

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Relevance estimators with calibrated confidence can detect when retrieved contexts are unhelpful and trigger abstention or parametric-knowledge fallback in RAG. | Reranking with a learned relevance score, trained via weak supervision from QA likelihood, improves both context selection and answer marginalization under noisy retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Evaluated only on single-hop open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA); generalization to multi-hop, multimodal, or adversarial poisoning settings is untested.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
authors: Yue Yu; Wei Ping; Zihan Liu; Boxin Wang; Jiaxuan You; Chao Zhang; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Unifying context reranking with answer generation in a single instruction-tuned LLM improves robustness to noisy retrieved contexts. | A small fraction of ranking data integrated into instruction tuning can outperform dedicated rerankers trained on much larger ranking corpora. | Reranking the top-N retrieved passages to a refined top-k mitigates the recall-vs-noise trade-off that hurts generation quality.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on single-round retrieval with text-only QA; does not address multimodal evidence, adversarial poisoning, or calibrated abstention, so should not be overclaimed as a general robustness solution.

title: ReDeEP: Detecting Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Mechanistic Interpretability
authors: ZhongXiang Sun; Xiaoxue Zang; Kai Zheng; Jun Xu; Xiao Zhang; Weijie Yu; Yang Song; Han Li
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RAG models can hallucinate even when retrieved evidence is accurate and relevant, due to overreliance on parametric knowledge in later-layer FFNs and insufficient retention of external context by copying attention heads. | Mechanistic interpretability can decouple a model's use of external evidence versus parametric knowledge, providing diagnostic signals for hallucination detection in RAG. | Detection-time interventions that reweight attention heads and FFN contributions can mitigate hallucinations without parameter updates.
limitation_or_note: Experiments focus on LLaMA-2/3 families and assume accurate retrieved context, so generalization to noisy/adversarial retrieval and larger or non-decoder architectures is not fully demonstrated.

title: Reliable Decision‑Making via Calibration‑Oriented Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
authors: Chaeyun Jang; Deukhwan Cho; Seanie Lee; Hyungi Lee; Juho Lee
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Calibration-oriented reranking can align RAG confidence with empirical decision correctness, mitigating overconfidence when retrieved evidence is unreliable. | Training a forecasting function over query-document pairs enables selective retrieval and query reformulation when no candidate passage provides sufficient decision support.
limitation_or_note: Relies on a surrogate LLM user model and GPT-4o-mini grading, so calibration claims depend on these proxies; synthetic supervision generation adds nontrivial overhead.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
benchmark_or_task: long_context_doc
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Self-reflection-based routing between RAG and long-context inference can preserve answer quality while substantially reducing cost. | Systematic failure analysis shows RAG struggles with multi-hop, general, complex, and implicit queries, motivating adaptive control under unreliable retrieved evidence. | Long-context LLMs and RAG produce highly overlapping predictions, supporting hybrid routing strategies for robust generation.
limitation_or_note: Self-Route assumes LLMs are well-calibrated in judging answerability; results depend on prompt design and may not transfer to adversarial or poisoned evidence settings.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
authors: Jiaqi Wei; Hao Zhou; Xiang Zhang; Di Zhang; Zijie Qiu; Noah Wei; Jinzhe Li; Wanli Ouyang; Siqi Sun
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Test-time critique-driven refinement can correct reasoning misalignment between LLM outputs and retrieved evidence, improving faithfulness under noisy retrieval. | Training a dedicated Critic Language Model via contrastive critique synthesis mitigates self-bias and outperforms larger self-critic baselines. | Dynamic stopping mechanisms (autonomous variants) enable adaptive refinement steps without sacrificing accuracy, addressing efficiency-robustness tradeoffs in RAG.
limitation_or_note: The 'robustness to noisy retrieval' claims are mostly QA-focused and the failure analysis shows the critic can hallucinate when retrieval is incomplete, so survey should not overclaim general robustness beyond QA settings.

title: Retrieving, Rethinking and Revising: The Chain-of-Verification Can Improve Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Chain-of-verification with scoring, judgment, and query revision can correct unreliable retrieval evidence via adaptive re-retrieval in RAG. | Joint training of QA and verification with CoT rationales improves generation consistency when references are imperfect.
limitation_or_note: Training data quality depends on GPT-4 synthesis and verification annotations; verification is effectively single-round in deployment and may not generalize beyond open-domain QA.

title: SEER: Self-Aligned Evidence Extraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Model-based evidence extraction with self-aligned learning can outperform heuristic context filtering by jointly optimizing faithfulness, helpfulness, and conciseness of extracted evidence. | Listwise-aware preference optimization (LPO) over model-sampled evidence candidates improves downstream RAG QA accuracy while substantially reducing input context length. | Evidence extractors fine-tuned via self-alignment show improved robustness to irrelevant/noisy retrieved passages compared to base extractors.
limitation_or_note: Limited to mid-scale LLMs and a single dense retriever; the expert design still requires domain choices, and robustness gains do not hold uniformly across all noise levels and datasets.

title: SePer: Measure Retrieval Utility Through The Lens Of Semantic Perplexity Reduction
authors: Lu Dai; Yijie Xu; Jinhui Ye; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Semantic perplexity reduction can quantify retrieval utility as belief shift in the generator, providing finer-grained signal than lexical match or NDCG-style metrics. | Evaluation of RAG should jointly consider retrieval quality and the LLM's prior knowledge, since irrelevant or already-known evidence yields zero utility. | Partial or intermediate evidence in multi-hop RAG can be diagnosed via knowledge-gain metrics rather than end-to-end accuracy alone.
limitation_or_note: Metric requires gold answers and Monte-Carlo sampling; does not itself defend against poisoned or adversarial evidence, only diagnoses utility.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
benchmark_or_task: other
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Systematic empirical comparison of RAG pipeline modules (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization) yields actionable best practices balancing accuracy and latency. | Fine-tuning generators with a mixture of relevant and randomly-selected documents improves robustness to irrelevant retrieved context while preserving utilization of relevant evidence. | Hybrid sparse-dense retrieval combined with HyDE and reranking (e.g., monoT5) improves evidence quality for downstream generation.
limitation_or_note: Best-practice recommendations are dataset- and model-specific (Llama2-7B-Chat on selected QA/fact-checking benchmarks); generalization to adversarial poisoning or systematically misleading evidence is not directly evaluated.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Akari Asai; Zeqiu Wu; Yizhong Wang; Avirup Sil; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Self-reflection tokens enable adaptive retrieval and on-demand grounding decisions, improving robustness when evidence is unnecessary or unreliable. | Critique tokens for relevance and support provide a fine-grained mechanism to filter retrieved passages and enforce faithfulness during decoding. | Controllable inference via weighted reflection-token scoring allows trading off citation precision, fluency, and retrieval frequency at test time.
limitation_or_note: Reflection tokens are distilled from GPT-4 judgments and the method is not directly evaluated against adversarial or poisoned retrieval contexts.

title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
authors: Jingsheng Gao; Linxu Li; Ke Ji; Weiyuan Li; Yixin Lian; yuzhuo fu; Bin Dai
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Joint RL-based optimization of when-to-retrieve, query rewriting, and answer generation outperforms separately trained RAG modules. | Reward shaping with retrieval cost penalties enables adaptive retrieval that avoids unhelpful or unreliable database queries. | Policy networks can learn to abstain from retrieval when the knowledge base lacks relevant evidence, improving cost-quality tradeoffs.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on open-domain QA with Bing search and does not explicitly study adversarial or poisoned evidence; robustness to unreliable evidence is implicit rather than measured.

title: TRACE the Evidence: Constructing Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
benchmark_or_task: graph_kg
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Constructing knowledge-grounded reasoning chains from retrieved documents can filter noise and improve multi-hop RAG performance under unreliable evidence. | Finer-grained KG triples plus autoregressive chain construction help identify and integrate dispersed supporting evidence more reliably than raw document concatenation. | Adaptive chain termination and grounding selections in KG options mitigate hallucination and irrelevant context propagation in RAG readers.
limitation_or_note: Evidence-quality gains are measured only via downstream QA; KG/chain quality is not directly evaluated, and the method assumes accessible token logits and Wikipedia-style title-text documents.

title: The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RAG systems are vulnerable to prompt-based extraction attacks that leak private retrieval database contents. | Integrating retrieval data can paradoxically reduce LLM training-data memorization leakage, while introducing new retrieval-side privacy risks. | Mitigations such as reranking, summarization, and distance thresholds offer partial defenses with privacy-utility tradeoffs.
limitation_or_note: Results are limited to two datasets and a few LLM/embedding combinations; defense evaluations are preliminary and may not generalize.

title: Training Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering through Backtracking Correction
authors: Huawen Feng; ZekunYao; Junhao Zheng; Qianli Ma
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Training LLMs with stepwise self-correction can improve robustness to noisy retrieved documents in RAG without requiring extensive external annotations. | Reformulating RAG as a multi-step decision-making process with backtracking enables models to better assess document relevance and avoid being misled by irrelevant evidence.
limitation_or_note: Method evaluated only on open-domain QA datasets with relatively short documents; generalization to other RAG scenarios like long-context or multimodal is not validated.

title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
authors:
Zongmeng Zhang, Yufeng Shi, Jinhua Zhu, Wengang Zhou, Xiang Qi, Peng Zhang, Houqiang Li;
    Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:59827-59850
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: RL-based alignment can train retrieval-augmented LLMs to prioritize retrieved context over parametric memory in knowledge-conflict settings | Reward shaping with KL and anti-collapse penalties enables trustworthy grounding without explicit supervision on how to respond
limitation_or_note: Assumes retrieved evidence contains the correct answer; performance depends on inherent instruction-following capacity of base model and may not handle imperfect retrieval well without modification.

title: Understanding Parametric and Contextual Knowledge Reconciliation within Large Language Models
authors: Jun Zhao; Yongzhuo Yang; Xiang Hu; Jingqi Tong; Yi Lu; Wei Wu; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuanjing Huang
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: LLMs route contextual and parametric knowledge through distinct sets of attention heads, with competition occurring within knowledge types rather than across them. | Conflicting evidence persists in residual streams without erasure, while aligned multi-source signals accumulate superpositionally to determine output selection. | Entity-aware probing can mechanistically diagnose how RAG models reconcile knowledge conflicts between retrieved context and parametric memory.
limitation_or_note: Experiments rely on synthetic counterfactual entity substitution and decoder-only LLaMA/Qwen models; generalization to naturally occurring conflicts and other architectures is untested.

title: Unified Active Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Adaptive/active retrieval that decides when to retrieve is essential for robust RAG, since indiscriminate retrieval can inject irrelevant or harmful evidence. | Multifaceted retrieval-timing criteria (intent, knowledge need, time-sensitivity, self-knowledge) outperform single-criterion approaches like FLARE, Self-RAG, and SKR. | Lightweight plug-and-play classifiers over frozen LLM hidden states enable efficient routing decisions with negligible inference overhead.
limitation_or_note: Limited to single-step retrieval and short-form generation; classifiers may not generalize OOD beyond evaluated scenarios.

title: Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
benchmark_or_task: not_applicable
metrics_reported_or_relevant: high
actual_contribution: Unsupervised training can teach LLMs to act as information refiners that integrate parametric knowledge with retrieved evidence under varied quality conditions. | Training LLMs to handle three retrieval scenarios (complete, incomplete/incorrect, and irrelevant retrieved texts) improves RAG robustness to noisy and misleading evidence. | Information refinement training enhances zero-shot RAG performance across diverse tasks while preserving generalization.
limitation_or_note: Experiments limited to 7B/13B LLaMA-2 models; the scenario taxonomy is synthetic rather than from real-world noisy retrieval, which may overestimate robustness gains.
